title: Make catalog continuation validation proportional to the page instead of the full filtered set
outcome: Exploratory ls uses live keyset continuations with work proportional to the requested page, an explicitly historical first-page total and an honest project-change notice. Compact next ProjectCut navigation and claim --under retain their existing exact server-side behavior.
acceptance: After the candidate-selection prerequisite, exploratory ls continuation pages seek after the carried ID or ready (priority, ID) tuple without a complete membership/count scan, including when the anchor was removed or reprioritized; a large-set counter and SQLite-work regression measures page-proportional work.

Exploratory ls does not refuse membership/order changes. It labels the first-page total historical, and project-head movement emits a notice that pages may differ and a fresh listing gives a newer view, without claiming proven filtered-membership changes.

Catalog/CLI documentation and behavioral tests state live-pagination limits: ID-order inserts before the anchor can be missed; ready-order movers can repeat or be missed. Compact next ProjectCut invalidation, project/filter/time guards, and claim --under selection remain unchanged.
